newsitem.title: HUNGARY: CZECH TV NOVA'S PARENT LOSES IN HUNGARIAN BIDS.
newsitem.headline: CZECH TV NOVA'S PARENT LOSES IN HUNGARIAN BIDS.

text.p: Hungary's National Television and Radio Board (ORTT) on Monday decided to award the franchises for Hungary's two new commercial TV channels to Swedish-Hungarian consortium MTM-SBS and a consortium led by CLT, which owns Radio et Television de Luxembourg (RTL).
U.S.-based Central European Media Enterprises (CME), parent of Czech TV Nova, failed in both its bids for the two channels, ORTT told Hungarian news agency MTI.
ORTT spokeman Gyorgy Lovas, confirming the news to Reuters, said the bids had been "very close".
"One important factor in the decision was the future diversity of Hungary's media scene," he said. "The decision was unanimous but for one abstention."
The ten-year concessions for two national commercial TV channels were on offer for eight billion forints plus 25 per cent VAT each, three years payable in advance.
The CLT led copnsortium, Magyar RTL, is owned by a consortium of CLT-UFA, Raiffeisen Unicbank, the UK Pearson group , publisher of the Financial Times, and Hungarian telecom company Matav.
MTM-SBS is a consortium of the Hungarian-registered company MTM Kommunikacios Rt, TeleMunchen and the majority US-owned company Scandinavian Broadcasting System.
The losing CME-led consortium is made up of US-based Central Media Enterprises and Hungarian companies, Mediacom, Intercom and DDTV Kft.
ORTT said last Wednesday it had been unable to select the winning bidders as there was not the necessary two-thirds majority of board members to pass any of the three bids.
Five of the eight-person board are delegated by opposition parties, two other members are delegated by the ruling parties while the president of the board is neutral.

The decision brings to an end seven years of political wrangling which has left Hungary's media privatisation trailing behind other former communist countries such as Poland and the Czech Republic, which already have commercial national television stations.
